s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent pleural effusion with lymphocytic predominance in a patient with a history of empiric treatment for presumed extrapulmonary tuberculosis
salient_findings: Negative cultures and stains for infectious organisms
key_facts: 84-year-old Asian man
Admitted with dyspnea
Empiric RIPE treatment started nine months earlier for presumed extrapulmonary tuberculosis
Initial colonoscopic biopsy showed granulomas with acid-fast stain–positive organism
Subsequent biopsies and sputum cultures were negative
QuantiFERON-TB Gold testing was negative
Developed dyspnea, cough, and weakness four weeks after starting RIPE
Thoracentesis yielded exudative, lymphocyte-predominant fluid with red color
Pleural fluid showed lymphocytosis (96%), exudative protein and LDH, and low complement activity
Multiple pleural biopsies showed inflammation without granulomata
Serum testing revealed an ANA titer of 1:160 with a speckled pattern

raw.syndrome_frame: Recurrent pleural effusion with lymphocytic predominance in a patient with a history of empiric treatment for presumed extrapulmonary tuberculosis
salient_findings: Negative cultures and stains for infectious organisms
key_facts: 84-year-old Asian man
Admitted with dyspnea
Empiric RIPE treatment started nine months earlier for presumed extrapulmonary tuberculosis
Initial colonoscopic biopsy showed granulomas with acid-fast stain–positive organism
Subsequent biopsies and sputum cultures were negative
QuantiFERON-TB Gold testing was negative
Developed dyspnea, cough, and weakness four weeks after starting RIPE
Thoracentesis yielded exudative, lymphocyte-predominant fluid with red color
Pleural fluid showed lymphocytosis (96%), exudative protein and LDH, and low complement activity
Multiple pleural biopsies showed inflammation without granulomata
Serum testing revealed an ANA titer of 1:160 with a speckled pattern

shortlist.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive ANA titer and speckled pattern, consistent with autoimmune disease

shortlist.label: Drug-induced lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient on RIPE treatment, which includes isoniazid, rifampin, and pyrazinamide, known to cause drug-induced lupus

shortlist.label: Tuberculous pleurisy
shortlist.why_kept: Initial colonoscopic biopsy showed granulomas with acid-fast stain–positive organism, suggesting tuberculosis

shortlist.label: Paradoxical tuberculous effusion
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed effusion while on RIPE treatment, consistent with paradoxical reaction

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphocytic predominance in pleural fluid and inflammation without granulomata, consistent with sarcoidosis

raw.rationale: The patient developed symptoms consistent with lupus erythematosus, such as pleural effusion and positive ANA titer, after starting RIPE treatment, which includes isoniazid, a known cause of drug-induced lupus.

rejected.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and positive ANA titer appeared after starting RIPE treatment, suggesting a drug-induced rather than systemic cause.

rejected.label: Tuberculous pleurisy
rejected.why: The patient's pleural fluid cultures were negative, and the QuantiFERON-TB Gold test was also negative, making tuberculous pleurisy less likely.

rejected.label: Paradoxical tuberculous effusion
rejected.why: Although the patient was diagnosed with a paradoxical tuberculous effusion initially, the subsequent negative cultures and lack of granulomata on pleural biopsies make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and biopsy results do not show granulomata, which are characteristic of sarcoidosis.
